name: Isolated Anencephaly

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Prenatal Diagnostic Criteria for Anencephaly

criteria.description: Absence of the cranial vault with exposed brain tissue
Absence or severe malformation of the forebrain (cerebrum and cerebellum)
Prenatal ultrasound showing absent cranial bones and brain structures

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of absent cranial vault and absence of forebrain on clinical or prenatal imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is typically made prenatally or immediately after birth due to characteristic cranial malformations.

laboratory: Elevated maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) levels during pregnancy
imaging: Prenatal ultrasound showing absent cranial vault and brain tissue
MRI confirming absence of cerebral hemispheres and skull bones
other: Physical examination revealing absence of skull and exposed brain tissue at birth

distinguishingFeatures: Involvement of both cranial and spinal neural tube defects
Open spinal defect with exposed spinal cord
Presence of herniated brain tissue covered by skin or membrane
Intact cranial vault except at herniation site

redFlags: Absence of cranial vault on prenatal imaging
Exposed malformed brain tissue at birth
references: Copp AJ, Stanier P, Greene ND. Neural tube defects: recent advances, unsolved questions, and controversies. Lancet Neurol. 2013 Aug;12(8):799-810.
Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). Facts about Anencephaly. 2021.
